utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Will the registrar please call the case?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Case number IT-97-25-PT, the Prosecutor versus Milorad Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. May we have the appearances?

utterances.speaker: MR. UERTZ-RETZLOFF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. For the Prosecution, we have today, to my left, Mrs. Peggy Kuo, and my name is Hildegard Uertz-Retzloff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. The lead counsel is Attorney Mihajlo Bakrac present here today with Attorney Miroslav Vlasic as legal counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. The accused, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The present hearing is for a motion by the Prosecution on protective measures filed on the 16th of June, and the Defence did respond to the motion by the Defence on the 10th of July. I would like to find out if there is anything more that the Prosecution would like to say about the motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. UERTZ-RETZLOFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, requested is only a general measure to grant confidentiality in the pre-trial stage. Similar measures have been granted by this Tribunal on several occasions. Also, from this Trial Chamber, the decision of the Kunarac case dated 29 April, 1998 is about the same subject. However, in this subject matter, we gave specifics, I think, which are important here to mention. Firstly, I refer to the Prosecutor's motion to preserve evidence dated 16 June, 1998 in which it was described that the accused was in the possession of a false I.D. card. The accused seems to have connections to criminal individuals who can provide false I.D. cards of a very high quality. Secondly, I refer to a decision of the Registrar dated 13 July, 1998 restricting the accused's contacts within the detention unit. It says, "Taking into account that there are reasonable grounds for believing that Mr. Milorad Krnojelac may interfere with the administration of justice." I think these are two additional points which I want to mention which makes it necessary to have this motion granted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Any response, besides what is in the response to the motion, by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we wish to add the following to that which has already been written: This request of the Prosecutor greatly reduces the right to the Defence which is guaranteed by Articles 21 and 22 of the Statute, because this request of the Prosecutor, to acquaint only the accused and his legal counsel with the content, considerably reduces the scope of defensibility and the rights involved. Also, it was said that the family of the accused could not become familiar with the statements that indict the accused in this trial. This has made far more difficult the accumulation of evidence by the Defence, because it is only the accused that Defence counsel can deal with, and especially from the point of view of this time distance. I think that because the family is aware of the circumstances in which the accused lived and, also, particularly, the time of the indictment, I think that the family could help Defence counsel accumulate the necessary material. Of course, I do agree that protective measures have to exist, and we shall seek the same for our own witnesses, that is to say, that the name and identity of a person who is testifying should not be disclosed. But if the contents itself cannot be disclosed, then this considerably reduces the scope of the possibilities extended by the Defence counsel. This is in the Statute, too. The Kunarac case is not a relevant case in point, because this is a rape case, and it really doesn't match, in any way, the indictment against Mr. Krnojelac. I believe that such a proposal of the Prosecutor should be refused to the extent to which it precludes the Defence the possibility of communicating with the family of the accused, because the contents of statements are very important for the Defence as well. This is also in keeping with the Statute of the Tribunal. That is all I wish to say at this point. I believe that such a proposal made by the Prosecutor should be refused and that Defence should be allowed to prepare rebuttal evidence in the best possible way. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, Mr. Defence Counsel, your concern is that the exclusion of the family of the accused from knowing the contents of the witness statements, that is what is worrying you, because you feel that that restricts the ability of the Defence to prepare the actual defence for the trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour, for the simple reason that I am an attorney from Belgrade, and the accused is from Foca, and the accused is the only person whom I can deal with. If I cannot deal with anyone else, then my hands are tied, too, to a large extent. I am not in a position equal to that of the Prosecutor. Of course, we all know that there have been cases of abusing the contents of witness statements here, and that they were even given to the media, and I certainly agree with that, but such a case should not tie the hands of the Defence in all future cases. You see, this is a negative example, which I can only condemn, but the contents of a statement have to be presented to the next of kin, the people who are the closest of all to the accused, so that we, on the other hand, could gather evidence which suits the purposes of the Defence, so to speak. If you deny this motion, the Defence can exclusively and only talk to the accused and also from this time distance and in this situation that he is in now. Why could I not gather evidence and show something to the wife of the accused and to his sons, to show what the incriminating material is? Perhaps they will remember certain details which may serve the purposes of the Defence. If you prevent me from doing so, then the Prosecutor and the Defence are not going to be in a position of equality. Also, the Statute cannot be observed if you act in this way. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Counsel. I think your concerns have been ably expressed, and the Chamber will take time to consider as to what exceptions to make to the motion of the Prosecution. A written decision will be issued later. In these open proceedings, is there anything else, Ms. Prosecutor? Anything else, Mr. Defence Counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: One more thing, Your Honour. As we have taken care of this issue, there's another thing which I also consider to be of great importance, and that is the translation of evidence. According to the new Rules, it is the Prosecutor who is supposed to take care of that. We have obtained, so far, one-third of the evidence material which we got from the registry. However, two-thirds of the material we have not received yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: May I interrupt you, Mr. Defence Counsel? I think we shall go into closed session to discuss the preparations of the trial. Those matters which you're raising now shall be in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In view of the fact that the matters for the motion are dealt with, the Court will adjourn and move into closed session for a Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: 2.40 p.m., to be reconvened sine die
